metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Essex County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Verona Park & Lanning Section, Forest Avenue & Sunset Ridge
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 3.12%, with an equalization ratio of 79.5%.
Public education represents 57.8% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 26.2%.
Average residential assessment is $496,875, producing an average annual tax bill of $15,502.5.

neighborhoods.name: Verona Park & Lanning Section
neighborhoods.character: Picturesque suburban community surrounding 54-acre Verona Park lake, with tree-lined avenues, colonials, and walk-to-school streets
neighborhoods.description: Charming residential borough between First and Second Watchung Mountains, prized for Verona Park boating and community sports.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High school levy proportion (57.8%) reflects high community prioritization of K-12 education.

neighborhoods.name: Forest Avenue & Sunset Ridge
neighborhoods.character: Elevated residential streets with charming pre-war colonials, cape cods, and views of the Watchung Mountains
neighborhoods.description: Family-centric neighborhood convenient to F.N. Brown and Forest Avenue elementary schools.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Consistent assessment valuations with low tax appeal litigation.

equityAnalysis.summary: Verona Township maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Verona Township, homeowners pay an average of $15,502.5 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 11.37% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 79.5%, assessed values average ~79.5% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 57.8% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 26.2%, and Essex County claims 16.0%.
